thesis_summary.thesis: Hawaiian Electric Industries is the parent of Hawaii's regulated electric utility and related businesses serving most of the state. **[Fact]** Consolidated revenues were about **$3.09 billion** in fiscal 2025 (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260227_rpt20251231_acc0000354707_26_000008.htm`). **[Fact]** The company reports an **Electric Utility** segment plus **All Other** activities. **[Fact]** Earnings and cash flow are set largely by the Hawaii Public Utilities Commission through allowed returns on rate-base capital, not by open-market pricing alone. **[Fact]** The common dividend has been suspended since the August 2023 Maui wildfires while the company funds legal and restoration obligations. **[Fact]** HE completed the sale of its **90.1%** stake in American Savings Bank at the end of calendar 2024 and is now essentially a pure-play utility (**[Inference]** from Horizon Kinetics Q1 2025 commentary, context tier).
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The stock still trades like a distressed credit event at roughly **$13** per share (Stooq, 2026-06-03), down sharply from pre-fire levels. **[Inference]** Index and income funds that sort on dividend yield never see the name, which creates a **predictive attribute** (Horizon Kinetics equity yield curve): the payoff is known in direction (regulated recovery, dividend reinstatement, credit repair) but mis-timed for twelve-month holders. **[Inference]** The market may be anchoring on trough GAAP earnings (**$0.71** diluted EPS in FY2025 per 10-K XBRL) instead of mid-cycle owner cash once wildfire payments normalize. **[Opinion]** Patience is the edge; precision on timing and residual liability is not.
